cases.name: lrgb_mono_ngc7635
cases.golden_note: Frozen floor re-cut 2026-09-08 for v5.0.4.0. ONE attributed cause, measured on this corpus: per-frame sky normalisation, which this release adds. This session's sky level spans -10.41 to +9.45 noise sigma across its 65 frames and 63 of the 65 are corrected, so until now every frame entered the per-voxel fit on its own level and a per-FRAME effect was being modelled per-PIXEL. Single variable, same build, normalize_frames off versus on, driven headless through StackingEngine with no PixInsight in the loop: stacked pixel-scale noise -- MAD of horizontal nearest-neighbour differences over background pixels, which is blind to the smooth gradients that would otherwise dominate -- fell 0.00099188 -> 0.00023288. That is a 4.26x reduction, worth roughly eighteen times the exposure, and it is the largest single improvement measured on this corpus. It is also the corpus previously measured at 5.19x the pixel-scale noise of a plain Huber estimator on identical voxels, with 26.9x of effective exposure thrown away; normalising the fit's INPUTS recovers most of that, which is direct evidence the bimodality the GMM was coin-flipping on was per-frame level variation rather than anything per-pixel. The change is proven an exact no-op where there is nothing to correct: HEAD (74fcf09) against this build with normalisation off hashes bit-identically (9941339b3f71f0e4...) over a real 8-frame stack, so everything that moved here is attributable to normalisation and to nothing else. All four primary hashes AND all three sweeps moved, which is expected and differs from the v5.0.3.1 re-cut: there only VeraLux's auto_tune moved and GHS/MTF/ArcSinh stayed bit-identical, because the stacked pixels were unchanged. Here the stacked pixels themselves change, so every stretch of them changes too. Do not re-cut this floor without the same kind of measurement.

cases.name: mono_lrgb_m27_2025
cases.alignment_note: 51 of 72 measured 2026-09-04. The 21 failures are the two temporal ends of a 7-hour session: chronological frames 0-19 and 66-71. Failure rate rises monotonically with distance from the reference (0-15 frames away: 31 ok / 0 failed; 32-39 away: 0 ok / 9 failed), and the reference is already the temporal midpoint, so this is cumulative tracking drift the single-reference matcher cannot bridge -- not filter, and not reference selection, which took this case from 1 of 72 to 51 of 72. Raise this floor when chained alignment lands.
cases.note: Re-enabled 2026-09-05. Phase B now carries a per-channel frame set: CacheSig gained a routing key so each mono filter gets its own cache, ShadowBuffers::n_frames is per channel, and global_frame_of maps each channel's local slot to the batch-global frame its FrameStats belong to. The golden for this case has never existed -- the previous one was deleted because it recorded three empty channels -- so it is generated fresh in this re-baseline.
